newsitem.title: USA: U.S Spot Prods-Prices surge with NYMEX, diffs ease.
newsitem.headline: U.S Spot Prods-Prices surge with NYMEX, diffs ease.

text.p: U.S. spot gasoline and distillate prices surged higher Monday, boosted by the rally in the futures market.
However, traders said spot market differentials across the U.S. appeared to weaken slightly in lackluster trading in reaction to the sharp gains on the NYMEX.
"It's a thin one here today, nothing to get too excited about," one Gulf Coast player said.
NYMEX June gasoline had rallied 1.61 cents while June heating oil was up 1.73 cents.

++ Gasoline differentials eased modestly Monday, with prompt conventional unleaded M1 barrels talked between about 3.70 to 3.80 cents under the June NYMEX, about 0.10 to 0.15 cent off late Friday levels.

Distillate differentials in the USG also showed little movement, with prompt No. 2 oil offered at 1.80 cents under the June NYMEX and prompt low sulphur diesel offered at 1.35 cents under the June NYMEX.
++ Gasoline differentials weakened, with prompt conventional M2 talked between 1.25 and 1.75 cents under the June NYMEX as buyers pulled back from the market.
Traders quoted prompt reformulated A2 gasoline offers at 1.30 cents over June futures, though barrels for delivery on the 20th of May were talked between 0.80 to 0.90 cent over June futures.
In the Midwest, differentials on Group Three low sulfur diesel narrowed about 0.75 cent to offers of 5.25 cents over June futures by midday Monday -- retreating as June NYMEX heating oil soared.

But diesel in the Chicago market eased only slightly to 4.75 cents over the print, traders said, holding firm amid continued five-to-ten-day delays by the Explorer Pipeline in deliveries of refined products from the Gulf Coast.

Group Three conventional unleaded gasoline diffs were stable at 4.0 cents over June futures in spite of a 1.46 cent increase in June NYMEX values, although Chicago diffs eased a half cent to 2.25 cents over.
